entries.reason: Covers all four tasks. Task 1: three groups with correct counts, Instantiated here (6), In this checkout (11) and Associated ↗ (1), which match the 6 root *.config.json files and the 17 entries in docs/_data/harness.json. Task 2: a Property / Value / Edit with / Source table with summarised values ('39 directories', '24 images', 'needs Bootstrap') and a 'Declared in cat-harness/cat-harness.json' line. Task 3: every row names a skill and has a ✎, and folioMount shows '⚠ no edit skill mapped: QA finding' instead of a blank. Task 4: the iHRIS entry carries a 'remote' badge, and the note says it is referenced, never materialized, nothing fetched, and that its ✎ opens litlfred/ihris. Gaps: the name, description and stub rows from the intent's table are missing (name appears only in the header), and there is no explicit 'Open ↗' control for the associated harness. The remote state is only described in a caption; no drawn state shows it.

Task 1 is not met. The sidebar has no 'in this checkout' group, so the 11 uninstantiated harnesses cannot be reached, and the instantiated group lists 5 harnesses with smart-trust missing, though smart-trust.config.json exists. Task 2 is partial. The Properties tab has no directories row: the 39 directories are moved to a 'Graphs (39)' tab, which also conflates directories with graphs. It also has no associatedHarnesses row, and name, description and stub are missing. Task 3 passes for the rows that are shown, including the folioMount QA finding, but associate-harness appears only in prose. Task 4 is partial: the 'Associated ↗' sidebar group and the 'remote' label are good, the associated entry has no ⚙, and the Associated tab is described rather than drawn.

At 1280 the list and the table sit side by side in one bordered region, so switching harnesses leaves the table in view, and the selected row is boxed and bold. The table has column headers, so the meaning of 'Edit with' is clear. Minor faults: the 'Source' header wraps to 'Sourc/e' because its column is too narrow, and the stray ⚙ on the selected C@T row has no function in this layout. The panel lives in the glass Settings under a Display / Harnesses switch, which adds one step from the sidebar divider, where a maintainer already is.

The ⚙ on each divider is a direct, discoverable entry point, and the modal is well laid out, with header, tabs and a readable four-column grid. However, the grid has no column headers, so the skill column and the ✎ column are unlabelled. The modal hides the list, so comparing two harnesses means close → ⚙ → reopen each time. The navbar intent says the sidebar is a 56 px strip at rest and the Harnesses group arrives folded, so the ⚙ buttons are two interactions deep and add a second control to every divider in chrome that is already dense.

At 390 the list drills into the detail view with a large '← Harnesses' back button. Table rows become labelled cards ('Property: / Value: / Edit with: / Source:'), there is no horizontal overflow (report.json: scrollWidth 390), and the QA finding stays bold inside its card. The cost is length: the page runs to about 1600 px for 9 properties, and the harness list is not visible on arrival, so the mobile entry state (the list) is not drawn.

The full-screen sheet renders without overflow, and × Close is a large target in the top right. But the sidebar is display:none at 390, so this wireframe shows no way to reach the sheet or to switch harnesses on a phone. The tabs wrap onto two lines. Property rows collapse into four unlabelled stacked lines (name, value, skill, ✎), so a reader has to infer which line is which, and the lone ✎ on its own line is a small target.

Good: a labelled region and nav, h2 labelled by aria-labelledby, a real table with an aria-label, list rows at least 44 px high, and the finding conveyed by text as well as ⚠. Faults: the ✎ links have no accessible name (a screen reader hears only '✎' or 'link'). The Display / Harnesses switches are spans with role=tab, so they are not focusable and have no tablist. The selection uses aria-current="page" where aria-current="true" (or aria-selected) is correct. On mobile the data-h pseudo-labels come from CSS ::before, which some screen readers do not announce once the table is display:block.

Good: role=dialog with aria-modal and aria-labelledby, 44 px ⚙ buttons each with a distinct aria-label ('Configure Bootstrap' and so on), a role=tablist, and ✎ links labelled 'Edit source'. Faults: the tabs are non-focusable spans, the tabpanel has no aria-labelledby, and the property rows are divs, so the property-to-skill relationship is lost to assistive tech. The ⚙ uses aria-expanded where a dialog opener should use aria-haspopup="dialog". The 'Edit source' labels are identical across rows and do not name the property. The associated entry has no focusable control at all.

Could borrow from B: add a per-divider ⚙ in the sidebar that opens this panel with that harness preselected (entry point from where the reader already is); give ✎ an aria-label naming the property; and draw the associated harness's selected state (remote badge, Open ↗, ✎ → litlfred/ihris) instead of a caption.

To reach intent-fit B needs an 'In this checkout (11)' group and smart-trust in the sidebar, the directories and associatedHarnesses rows back on Properties, and column headers. With those added it converges on A, only in a modal, and it still cannot compare harnesses side by side. Its useful ideas are the ⚙ entry point, the labelled 44 px buttons and a separate Associated tab. They transfer to A more easily than A's list transfers to B.

notes.A: Recommended. It is the only candidate that shows every harness in one place with correct counts and every intent row that matters (directories, associatedHarnesses). Before adoption: add the name/description/stub rows, draw the associated-harness detail state with an explicit Open ↗, label the ✎ links, make the tabs real buttons in a tablist, widen the Source column, and remove the stray ⚙.
notes.B: Not recommended as drawn: it fails task 1 (no checkout group, smart-trust missing) and drops the directories and associatedHarnesses rows. A hybrid is better than either candidate: A's grouped list and property table in the glass Settings, reached also from a B-style labelled ⚙ on each sidebar divider that opens A preselected. A would also take B's aria-labelled ✎ and 44 px buttons, and optionally an 'Associated' sub-view inside A's detail for harnesses that declare associations.
